text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA

- If Serbia does not urgently find a political solution through dialogue and recognition of election results Montengro will have to seriously consider its next moves, says Montenegrin Parliament Speaker Svetozar Marovic.
- Following police blockade of opposition protest marches on Orthodox Christmas Day, opposition plans to organise protest car drives through the city again.
- Students of Novi Sad to come to Belgrade on Thursday to join Belgrade students in their protest.
- Zajedno opposition leaders and representatives of protesting students invited to attend U.S. President Clinton's inauguration on January 20.

- The German Mark was worth a record five dinars on the street in Belgrade and in Podgorica on Tuesday (official exchange rate is 3.3 dinars) while the black market exchange rate continues to change from hour to hour.
- New meeting of former Yugoslavia successor states to be held in Brussels on January 16-17.

- Serbian trade minister Srdjan Nikolic to hold talks today with strike committee of the Belgrade Department Stores Company. Out of 45 stores within the company, workers at 14 have been on strike over unpaid wages.
- What will be the fate of 800,000 surplus workers in Yugoslavia?
POLITIKA
- Agrarian sector's participation in Serbia's 1997 budget is slightly reduced this year in relation to last, even though the budget was increased by 17.2 per cent from 1996.
- Law expected to be passed by end of March resolving National Bank of Yugoslavia's debt of 21.2 billion dinars ($4 billion) to commercial banks for frozen foreign currency reserves.
- New Democracy Party and city committee of the Socialist Party or Serbia condemn Monday's bombing of the headquarters of the Yugoslav United Left (JUL).
- Supporters of opposition coalition Zajedno in Kragujevac make enormous din to drown out evening news on Radio-Television Serbia.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Christmas marked in Orthodox churches in the country and abroad.
- New labour relations law takes effect in Serbia Wednesday, giving extended powers to directors of firms.
- Yugoslav airlines JAT expects foreign exchange earnings of $230 million in 1997 and 27 percent increase to 1.4 million in number of passengers compared with 1996.
- Drop of the dinar on the black market exchange rate has also pushed up street price of cigarettes and petrol.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- In the first days of its rule opposition in Novi Sad launches witchhunt against those who think differently.
- Number of suicides in Serbia doubled in 40 years according to official statistics.
